scientific_question: Is the memory-decline signal in CA1 astrocytic reactivity strongest specifically in astrocytes immediately adjacent to CA1 pyramidal neurons rather than across CA1 as a whole?
approach: Assign cells to CA1 using annotation polygons, then select CA1 Pyramidal Neuron, Astrocyte, and Reactive Astrocyte cells. For each CA1 astrocyte-lineage cell (Astrocyte or Reactive Astrocyte), determine whether at least one CA1 Pyramidal Neuron centroid lies within radius R. Compute the donor-level score as the reactive fraction within this peripyramidal astrocyte niche: reactive_astrocytes_near_pyramidal / (reactive_astrocytes_near_pyramidal + astrocytes_near_pyramidal).

variations.name: peripyramidal_reactivity_r25um
variations.description: Baseline: reactive fraction among CA1 astrocyte-lineage cells lying within 25 µm of at least one CA1 pyramidal neuron.

variations.name: peripyramidal_reactivity_r35um
variations.description: Local radius expansion to 35 µm to test whether the signal is tightly peripyramidal or slightly broader within the CA1 pyramidal field.

notes: Use SegmentationNode/centroids for geometry and ClassificationNode labels for cell identity. Region polygons in CustomAnnotations are stored at 16x cell coordinates, so divide polygon vertices by 16 before point-in-polygon assignment. A KD-tree or cKDTree on CA1 pyramidal centroids is adequate for radius queries. If convenient, convert µm to pixels using slide-specific Aperio MPP from the paired .svs; otherwise a fixed ~0.503 µm/pixel approximation is acceptable given the small cohort MPP spread. If CA1 is absent or the peripyramidal astrocyte-lineage denominator is too small for a stable fraction, return NaN.
rationale: Round 1 found a strong CA1 reactive-astrocyte fraction signal, so the right next test is a tighter niche version of the same biology rather than jumping to an unrelated summary. A peripyramidal astrocyte-reactivity biomarker could clarify whether the accepted signal is driven by neuron-adjacent gliosis, and it gives the evaluator a plausible cleaner replacement for the current panel member or a partly nonredundant addition if the local niche is sharper than the region-wide fraction.
